name: Automatic Anchors
description: Client-side JavaScript that generates HTML id attributes on configurable page elements (headings by default) and optionally inserts inline permalinks, so any section can be deep-linked.
project_description:
Automatic Anchors is a small utility module that generates HTML `id` attributes on a configurable list of matched page elements so that any section of a page can be linked to directly with a URL fragment (e.g. `/about#kevins-famous-chili`). By default it targets `h2`–`h6` headings anywhere in the page `body` and derives each id from the heading's own text, converting it to an i18n-friendly, hyphenated, lowercased, truncated (64-char) slug and de-duplicating collisions with a numeric suffix. It never overwrites an id that is already present, so manually authored anchors are preserved. It can additionally insert an inline permalink control (a small `#` link by default) inside each matched element to help editors and readers copy the direct URL to a section — the same behaviour seen in the Drupal developer documentation on drupal.org.

The entire mechanism runs in the browser: `hook_page_attachments()` attaches a jQuery library and passes the configuration through `drupalSettings`, and the bundled `auto_anchors.js` walks the DOM on the window `load` event, assigns ids, optionally appends the permalink links, and smooth-scrolls to the current `#hash` if one is present. Because id generation is client-side, the ids do not appear in the server-rendered HTML, are not present for non-JavaScript clients or crawlers, and are recomputed on every page load. The target elements are chosen by two admin-configurable comma-separated CSS-selector lists ("root elements" and "anchor elements"), so the module is not limited to node bodies or to headings.

Configuration lives at `/admin/config/auto_anchors/settings` behind the `administer automatic anchors` permission (marked `restrict access: true`). Visibility of the inline permalink control is gated per user by the `show automatic anchor links` permission. Admin pages are excluded by default. The module was featured as Module of the Week on the Talking Drupal podcast, episode #477.
